policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This is the first draft of the NIST AI RMF, published March 17, 2022. Part 3 was not yet developed at time of publication. The framework is explicitly voluntary and not a compliance mechanism; it is intended to be used alongside existing laws, regulations, and mandatory guidance. Developed under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283). Framework covers all sectors, organization sizes, and AI maturity levels.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance as a matter of ensuring trustworthy, safe, and reliable AI systems that do not harm individuals or society. Core language centers on managing adverse impacts, ensuring accuracy, safety, privacy, and mitigating harmful bias for end users and communities. Innovation enablement is a secondary frame, as the document argues that managing risk builds trust and enables broader AI adoption. Fundamental rights and social stability appear as additional concerns via references to civil liberties, fairness, equity, and societal risk.

evidence_spans.quote: Ensuring that these inferences are helpful and not harmful in particular use cases – especially when inferences are rapidly scaled and amplified – is fundamental to trustworthy AI.
